signatures.name: history read API (decision loop CAN read recorded exit codes)
signatures.snippet:
pub fn read_events(&self) -> Result<Vec<HistoryEvent>>
fn record_event(&mut self, run_id: Option<String>, step_id: Option<String>, kind: &str, payload: serde_json::Value, display: impl Into<String>) -> Result<()>

how_it_works: A RunCommand action is executed by execute_run_command (src/actions/mod.rs:947-993). It runs `sh -c <command>` and captures ground truth: `exit_code = output.status.code()` (line 968), and sets ActionStatus::Completed vs Failed strictly from `output.status.success()` (969-973). The exit_code, stdout, stderr are embedded into ActionResult.content as JSON (981-986); diagnostic is set to "command returned a non-zero exit status" on failure.

The exit code is captured in TWO places. (a) Fed back to the AGENT: the step loop pushes the ActionResult into request.action_results (src/app/mod.rs:4059), which is serialized into the next runtime turn's envelope as `action_results` (src/runtime/mod.rs:788) and `session_events`. (b) Recorded DURABLY by the HARNESS: record_command_completed_with_group (src/app/mod.rs:4753-4801) emits a `command_completed` history event with payload {action_id, command, status, exit_code, diagnostic}. So the answer to 'can the decision loop read the exit code, or only the agent?' is BOTH — it is durably recorded and readable via history.read_events() (src/history/mod.rs:180).

CRITICAL GAP: although the exit code is recorded as ground truth, the VERDICT is currently self-attested, never derived from it. When the (grader) agent finishes, it returns a RuntimeOutput::AgentResult whose `status` (AgentResultStatus::Completed/Failed/...) and free-text `verification` strings are chosen by the model. The harness accepts that result verbatim at src/app/mod.rs:3084-3092 (single agent) and src/app/mod.rs:2229-2230 (parallel child via record_parallel_child_result): it records an `agent_result` event from `serde_json::to_value(&result)` and pushes it into run.previous_results. No code compares the claimed status/verification against the recorded command_completed exit_code.

The runtime schema briefs that drive this self-attestation are identical across codex/claude/cursor (src/runtime/codex.rs:320-333, src/runtime/claude.rs:1001-1014, src/runtime/cursor.rs:1033-1046). They instruct the agent to fill `verification` with prose like 'how you confirmed the result, e.g. cargo test passed' and to pick `status` from the enum. AgentResult is then reconstructed from that JSON by parse_agent_result -> parse_contract (serde Deserialize), so every field including `status`/`verification` is model-controlled.

The next orchestrator decision is an LLM step too: previous_results (self-attested AgentResults) plus session_events (which DOES include command_completed with the real exit_code, preserved through compact_history_payload, src/app/mod.rs:5126-5131) are placed in its envelope (src/runtime/mod.rs:785-792). So the orchestrator could in principle read the exit code, but nothing programmatically grounds PASS in exit-0 — it is left to model judgment.

Harness-constructed terminal results already exist and bypass the agent: failed_agent_result (src/app/mod.rs:5976-5990), limit_reached_agent_result, cancelled_agent_result. These prove the harness can author/override an AgentResult's status deterministically — the same seam a derived verdict can use.
verdictGrounding.design_recommendation: Ground the grade in the recorded command_completed exit_code, not the agent's self-attested AgentResult.status/verification. Recommended shape: introduce a HARNESS-OWNED GraderVerdict record derived deterministically, kept OUT of the model-filled contract. Concretely: (1) Add a struct GraderVerdict { passed: bool, command: String, exit_code: Option<i64>, source_event_id: String, basis: enum {ExitCode, NoVerificationCommand, ToolError} } in src/orchestrator/mod.rs near AgentResult (124-160). Do NOT add it as a plain serde field on AgentResult that the agent fills — AgentResult is reconstructed by parse_agent_result/parse_contract (src/orchestrator/mod.rs:297-312), so any agent-writable field is still self-attested. If you attach it to AgentResult, mark it `#[serde(skip_deserializing, default)]` so only the harness can set it. (2) Derive it at the single-agent completion seam src/app/mod.rs:3083-3092 (and the parallel path at record_parallel_child_result, src/app/mod.rs:2229-2230) right before `run.previous_results.push(RunStepResult::Agent { result })`. The derivation source should be the durable command_completed events for this run_id+step_id (already written by record_command_completed_with_group, src/app/mod.rs:4753-4801) read via history.read_events() (src/history/mod.rs:180), or equivalently the in-memory request.action_results accumulated at src/app/mod.rs:4059 (whose ActionResult.content.exit_code / ActionStatus is the same ground truth from execute_run_command, src/actions/mod.rs:968-986). PASS requires that the designated verification command exists AND its recorded exit_code == 0 (mirror the existing `output.status.success()` logic at src/actions/mod.rs:969); otherwise FAIL/UNVERIFIED — never trust AgentResult.status alone. (3) Emit a new `grader_verdict` history event (use record_event, src/app/mod.rs:4164) so it is durable and visible in the projection, and so the next orchestrator decision can consume a harness-authored verdict rather than prose. (4) Identify WHICH command is the verification command via config (a grader-agent setting / expected grade command) rather than guessing, so an arbitrary passing `echo` cannot satisfy the gate. This reuses the existing event-sourcing pattern (record ground truth as an event, then derive), matches how failed_agent_result/limit_reached_agent_result already let the harness override status (src/app/mod.rs:5976-6004), and makes a fabricated `status: completed` / `verification: [\"cargo test passed\"]` non-load-bearing because PASS is computed from the recorded exit code.
gotchas: AgentResult.status and AgentResult.verification are fully model-controlled: they are deserialized from agent output by parse_agent_result -> parse_contract (src/orchestrator/mod.rs:297-312). A grader can emit status=completed with verification=["cargo test passed"] having run nothing. Do not gate on these.

The exit code IS already durable and readable by the decision loop — record_command_completed_with_group writes a `command_completed` event with exit_code/status/diagnostic (src/app/mod.rs:4787-4800) and history.read_events() returns it. The missing piece is purely the derivation/gate, not capture.

ActionStatus::Failed vs Completed is already derived from output.status.success() in execute_run_command (src/actions/mod.rs:969-973), but a non-zero exit only sets the ActionResult/diagnostic — it does NOT prevent the agent from subsequently returning AgentResultStatus::Completed. The two are decoupled today.

command_completed is suppressed for ApprovalRequired/Denied actions (src/app/mod.rs:4761-4766), and RunCommand can also be Denied by policy before execution (execute_action_request, src/actions/mod.rs:290-332, incl. VCS-mutation denial). A verdict deriver must treat 'no command_completed event / denied' as UNVERIFIED, not PASS.

Parallel children take a different completion path (record_parallel_child_result at src/app/mod.rs:2229-2230) and resumed approvals take resolve_pending_approval (src/app/mod.rs:1667-1686); both push action_results and AgentResults. Any verdict derivation must cover all three seams (single agent 3083, parallel child 2229, approval-resume 1679) or graders that run their command behind an approval will be ungraded.

session_events passed to the orchestrator are compacted (compact_history_payload, src/app/mod.rs:5126-5215). Scalar exit_code survives, but if you rely on the orchestrator LLM reading exit codes from session_events you inherit truncation and model-judgment risk — prefer a harness-computed grader_verdict event over LLM inference.

The agent only ever sees stdout/stderr/exit_code as text in the NEXT turn's action_results; it can mis-summarize them. Grounding must read the structured ActionResult.content.exit_code / the command_completed payload, not the agent's prose.

signatures.name: runtime_request (consumes agent_profile by VALUE)

how_it_works: The loop lives in drive_run_inner (src/app/mod.rs:1858-1868): it repeatedly calls run_orchestrator_step, and each OrchestratorDecision is fed to handle_orchestrator_decision, whose bool return is the loop continuation signal -- Ok(true) keeps looping (re-enter orchestrator), Ok(false) breaks. So a grader that wants the orchestrator to re-evaluate just needs to return true / leave run_state Running and add a result to previous_results.

handle_orchestrator_decision (1873-1952) matches decision.status. Only DecisionStatus::Continue dispatches work: it calls normalized_next_step() (orchestrator/mod.rs:247) to collapse schema v1 next_agent / v2 next_step into a DecisionNextStep, then routes SingleAgent -> handle_single_agent_decision or ParallelGroup -> handle_parallel_group_decision. Complete sets RunState::Completed + records run_completed and returns Ok(false); WaitingForUser parks a clarification; Failed sets RunState::Failed. Complete/WaitingForUser/Failed all return Ok(false) (loop ends).

handle_single_agent_decision (1954-1985) is the existing sentinel-route precedent: it first checks `next_agent_id == COUNCIL_WORKFLOW_AGENT_ID` (a magic agent id that is NOT a real AgentProfile), gates it through council_route_allowed (5535) against prompt+session_goal, and on success delegates to the virtual executor run_council_workflow instead of run_agent_step. Otherwise it applies review_fix_cycle_limit_reached and calls run_agent_step, mapping AgentStepOutcome::Completed -> Ok(true) and Paused/Stop -> Ok(false).

run_agent_step (3026-3095) is the leaf executor for one real agent. In the non-resume branch it enforces max_agent_steps (3040), increments run.step_count (3055), fetches the producing profile `let agent = self.agent(next_agent_id)?.clone()` (3052) and MOVES it into runtime_request (3063-3070). In the success path RuntimeOutput::AgentResult arm (3084-3095) it: (a) record_event "agent_result" with the serialized AgentResult, (b) `run.previous_results.push(RunStepResult::Agent { result })` (3092), (c) clear_active_step, (d) returns Ok(AgentStepOutcome::Completed).

Key scoping fact for a grader gate: at the AgentResult arm, the producing AgentProfile clone (`agent`, line 3052) is already MOVED into runtime_request, so it is NOT in scope. But `next_agent_id: &str` is a function parameter in scope for the whole body, so the gate can re-fetch via `self.agent(next_agent_id)` (4066, returns &AgentProfile) and call `.has_capability(&Capability::Edit)`. The changed-file signal is `result.changed_files` (orchestrator/mod.rs:155) -- but `result` is consumed by the push at line 3092, so the gate value must be computed (or changed_files cloned) BEFORE that push.

run_council_workflow (3155-3323) is the proven virtual-workflow executor template and maps 1:1 onto a grader: set RunState::Running; wall_clock_limit_reached guard; a serial `for member in members` loop; inside each iteration re-check wall-clock + `limit_reached(&self.config.limits.max_agent_steps, run.step_count)` (returning Ok(false)/LimitReached on breach), `run.step_count += 1`, emit agent_step_started, build a runtime_request with output_schema "agent_result", run it (here via tokio timeout + execute_runtime_step), and collect a report; after the loop it synthesizes one AgentResult, records agent_result/*_completed events, `run.previous_results.push(RunStepResult::Agent { result })`, and returns Ok(true) so the orchestrator loop continues.
dispatchLoop.design_recommendation: Recommended shape: a hybrid -- reuse run_council_workflow (src/app/mod.rs:3155-3323) as the EXECUTOR template, but TRIGGER it by force-injection at the run_agent_step AgentResult arm rather than as an orchestrator-routed sentinel. Concretely: (1) Add `async fn run_grading_workflow(&mut self, run: &mut RunDriveContext, producing_agent_id: &str, edited: &AgentResult) -> Result<()>` cloned structurally from run_council_workflow -- same RunState::Running + wall_clock_limit_reached guard, same `limit_reached(&self.config.limits.max_agent_steps, run.step_count)` check, `run.step_count += 1`, agent_step_started/agent_result/grading_completed events, and `run.previous_results.push(RunStepResult::Agent { result: grader_result })` so the grader verdict becomes ordinary prior context. (2) Inject the call in the AgentResult arm of run_agent_step between line 3092 (`run.previous_results.push(RunStepResult::Agent { result })`) and line 3094 (`Ok(AgentStepOutcome::Completed)`), gated by something like `let should_grade = self.agent(next_agent_id).map(|a| a.has_capability(&Capability::Edit)).unwrap_or(false) && !changed.is_empty();` -- compute `changed`/`should_grade` from `result.changed_files` BEFORE the push at 3092 (result is moved there). Do NOT loop inside run_agent_step: let it return Completed, and let the existing drive_run_inner loop (1858-1868) re-enter the orchestrator, which sees the grader's RunStepResult::Agent and decides whether to re-route to the editor/fixer -- this gives the grade->fix->re-grade loop for free and reuses the existing review_fix_cycle_limit_reached gate (1977) for cycle bounding. Rationale for force-injection over a `GRADER_WORKFLOW_AGENT_ID` sentinel routed like council (1960-1976 + council_route_allowed at 5535): an auto-grader should fire deterministically on every qualifying edit, not depend on the orchestrator electing to route to it; the gate inputs (changed_files + producing profile capability) are precisely available at run_agent_step but are LOST by the time a fresh orchestrator decision is normalized. Use the sentinel pattern only if you instead want the orchestrator to opt into grading on demand -- in that case mirror handle_single_agent_decision's council branch exactly (sentinel id check + a grading_route_allowed gate + delegate to run_grading_workflow returning Ok(true)/Ok(false)).
gotchas: At the AgentResult arm, `result` is MOVED by `run.previous_results.push(RunStepResult::Agent { result })` (src/app/mod.rs:3092). Any grader gate that needs result.changed_files / result.status / result.agent must read or clone them BEFORE line 3092, or refactor to bind the result first and push after grading.

The producing AgentProfile is NOT in scope at the AgentResult arm: the `let agent = self.agent(next_agent_id)?.clone()` at line 3052 lives only in the non-resume branch and is moved into runtime_request (3063-3070). To check has_capability(Edit) you must re-fetch `self.agent(next_agent_id)` (4066). Also note this profile fetch only happens on the non-resume path -- the resume path (3037-3038) reuses a prebuilt request and never touches the profile.

run_agent_step is reached from THREE call sites, not just handle_single_agent_decision: the resume paths in drive_run_inner (1828-1839 Agent resume) and the subtask path (1848-1854). Force-injecting grading inside run_agent_step's AgentResult arm will fire for ALL of them (including subtasks and council members route through run_council_workflow, which does NOT call run_agent_step -- council uses execute_runtime_step directly at 3247, so council members won't be auto-graded). Confirm whether subtask runs should be graded; if not, gate on run.subtask.is_none().

step_count is the shared budget: both run_agent_step (3055) and run_council_workflow (3221) increment run.step_count and both check `limit_reached(&self.config.limits.max_agent_steps, run.step_count)`. A grader step that increments step_count consumes the same max_agent_steps budget as real agent work and can itself trip LimitReached -- decide whether grading should be budget-exempt or share the budget.

COUNCIL_WORKFLOW_AGENT_ID = "council" (orchestrator/mod.rs:9) is a virtual id with no AgentProfile entry; handle_single_agent_decision special-cases it BEFORE the run_agent_step path, and self.agent("council") would error with 'missing required agent'. A grader sentinel id must be handled the same way (intercepted before agent lookup) and must not collide with any real `[agents.*]` key.

handle_orchestrator_decision's bool contract drives the loop: returning Ok(false) BREAKS the orchestrator loop (drive_run_inner 1861-1863). run_council_workflow returns Ok(true) on success specifically so the loop continues. A sentinel-routed grader must follow the same Ok(true)=keep-looping / Ok(false)=stop convention; an inline force-injected grader instead just needs to leave run_state == Running and return AgentStepOutcome::Completed so the caller maps it to Ok(true).

normalized_next_step (orchestrator/mod.rs:247) bails if a decision sets both next_agent and next_step, and schema_version 1 cannot select ParallelGroup. If grading is ever orchestrator-routed, route it as a SingleAgent next_step/next_agent only -- do not try to express it as a ParallelGroup under schema v1.

signatures.snippet:
// RawLimits (deny_unknown_fields): max_review_fix_cycles: Option<Limit>,  (469)
// merge: if let Some(value) = limits.max_review_fix_cycles { self.limits.max_review_fix_cycles = value; }  (972-974)

how_it_works: Two distinct limit families exist. (A) Per-step run cap: config `max_agent_steps` (Limit, default Value(12)) checked via the free fn `limit_reached(&self.config.limits.max_agent_steps, run.step_count)` at the top of every step-spawning path. (B) Cycle cap: config `max_review_fix_cycles` (Limit, default Value(2)) checked via `review_fix_cycle_limit_reached` which counts reviewer->fixer transitions in `run.previous_results`.

The reached-vs-stop split is the established pattern: a `*_reached(&self, ...) -> bool` predicate (e.g. wall_clock_limit_reached 3644, step_time_limit_reached 3662) plus a `stop_for_*(&mut self, ...) -> Result<()>` helper (3648, 3666, 3685) that sets `self.state.run_state = RunState::LimitReached` and records a `run_limit_reached`/`step_limit_reached` event. Callers invoke the predicate, then the stop helper, then return their own outcome variant.

For max_agent_steps this pattern is only partially applied. The batch parallel-group case HAS a predicate+stop pair (`parallel_group_exceeds_agent_step_limit` 2346 / `stop_for_parallel_group_agent_step_limit` 2357). But the four per-step sites (2399, 2895, 3040, 3208) inline the full body: `limit_reached(...)` guard, then 6 hand-copied lines (set state + record_event with json!({"limit":"max_agent_steps","value":run.step_count})), differing only in the trailing message string and the return expression (`break`, `OrchestratorStepOutcome::Stop`, `AgentStepOutcome::Stop`, `Ok(false)`). The 5th max_agent_steps reference (3772) is a guard inside schedule_parse_repair, not a stop — it just suppresses a repair attempt.

CONFIRMED: there is NO shared `stop_for_agent_step_limit` helper. grep for `stop_for_agent_step_limit` returns nothing; the only agent-step stop helper is the group-specific `stop_for_parallel_group_agent_step_limit`.

The review-fix cycle bound is hardcoded to the reviewer/fixer agent ids in two places: `review_fix_cycle_limit_reached` gates on `next_agent_id == "fixer"` (3705), and `review_fix_cycle_count` matches the literal strings "reviewer" and "fixer" (6024-6025). The serial call site (1977) forwards the real `next_agent_id`; the parallel call site (1993) passes the literal "fixer" and additionally scans `group.steps` for an agent == "fixer". The event payload's `limit` field is the literal "max_review_fix_cycles". There is NO grade-retry cycle concept anywhere (grep for grade/grader/grade_retry across src/ finds nothing).

Limit is a 2-variant enum (Value(u32)/Unlimited) with `is_reached_by` using `>=`; both the per-step and cycle paths route through `is_reached_by` (cycle via `limit_reached`, batch group via its own inline match at 2351-2354 that uses `>` on a saturating_add instead — a subtle inconsistency).
cycleLimits.design_recommendation: (a) Per-step helper: add a predicate+stop pair mirroring the existing family, next to stop_for_wall_clock_limit at src/app/mod.rs:3648. Add `fn agent_step_limit_reached(&self, run: &RunDriveContext) -> bool { limit_reached(&self.config.limits.max_agent_steps, run.step_count) }` and `fn stop_for_agent_step_limit(&mut self, run: &RunDriveContext, message: &str) -> Result<()> { self.state.run_state = RunState::LimitReached; self.record_event(Some(run.run_id.clone()), None, \"run_limit_reached\", json!({\"limit\": \"max_agent_steps\", \"value\": run.step_count}), message) }`. Pass `message` as a param because the only per-site variation is the trailing string. Then rewrite all four duplicated blocks (2399, 2895, 3040, 3208) to `if self.agent_step_limit_reached(run) { self.stop_for_agent_step_limit(run, \"<msg>\")?; <return/break>; }`, keeping each site's own control-flow expression (this matches how wall_clock callers already keep their own return). Reuse the predicate at the 3772 guard too (`if run.parse_repair_attempts >= 1 || self.agent_step_limit_reached(run)`), without the stop helper. This eliminates the 6th copy and centralizes the LimitReached+event mutation. Optionally fold the batch-group inline match (2351-2354) onto is_reached_by for consistency (note it currently uses `>` with saturating_add over the projected post-group count, so it must stay a separate batch predicate, but its stop body could share the event-shape).\n(b) Generalize the cycle bound beyond the hardcoded \"fixer\": (1) Generalize `review_fix_cycle_count` (src/app/mod.rs:6019) into `fn cycle_count(results: &[RunStepResult], open_agent: &str, close_agent: &str) -> u32` with the same saw_open/close accumulation but comparing `result.agent` to the params. Keep `review_fix_cycle_count` as a thin call `cycle_count(results, \"reviewer\", \"fixer\")` or replace its callers. (2) Introduce a small table of bounds, e.g. `struct CycleBound { limit_field: fn(&Limits) -> &Limit, label: &'static str, open_agent: &'static str, close_agent: &'static str }` with entries for review-fix (reviewer->fixer, max_review_fix_cycles) and grade-retry (e.g. grader->fixer or grader->reviser, a new max_grade_retry_cycles). (3) Replace `review_fix_cycle_limit_reached(run, next_agent_id)` (3704) with `fn cycle_limit_reached(&self, run, next_agent_id) -> Option<&CycleBound>` that returns the first bound whose `close_agent == next_agent_id` AND `limit_reached(bound.limit, cycle_count(run.previous_results, bound.open_agent, bound.close_agent))`. (4) Make `stop_for_review_fix_cycle_limit` (3712) take the bound so the event `limit`/`value` are parameterized (`json!({\"limit\": bound.label, \"value\": cycle_count(...)})`). (5) Update both call sites: serial (1977) `if let Some(bound) = self.cycle_limit_reached(run, next_agent_id) { self.stop_for_cycle_limit(run, bound)?; return Ok(false); }`; parallel (1993) iterate `group.steps` and check each `step.agent` against `cycle_limit_reached(run, &step.agent)` instead of the literal \"fixer\". (6) Add config plumbing for the new bound: `max_grade_retry_cycles: Limit` in Limits (src/config/mod.rs:178) + Default (190, e.g. Value(1)), RawLimits field (469), and merge block (972). Tests to update: review_fix_cycle_count_skips_initial_fixer_pass (src/app/mod.rs:11321) and the toml fixture max_review_fix_cycles=1 (11401) / config defaults asserts in src/config/mod.rs.
gotchas: The 5th cited location (src/app/mod.rs:3772) is NOT a stop block — it is a guard inside schedule_parse_repair that returns Ok(false) (suppresses a repair) when steps are exhausted. A shared stop helper must NOT be applied here; only the predicate part (agent_step_limit_reached) is reusable.

The batch parallel-group check at 2351-2354 uses `run.step_count.saturating_add(group.steps.len()) > limit` (strict `>` on projected count), whereas every per-step site uses `is_reached_by` (`>=` on current count). These are intentionally different (pre-flight vs per-step) — do not collapse the group predicate into the per-step helper or you change semantics.

record_event vs record_event_with_group: the four per-step duplicates use `record_event` (no group); the group stop helper uses `record_event_with_group`. A shared per-step helper should use plain record_event; the group path stays separate.

Each duplicated block ends with a DIFFERENT control-flow expression (break / OrchestratorStepOutcome::Stop / AgentStepOutcome::Stop / Ok(false)). Follow the existing wall_clock convention: the stop helper returns Result<()> and the CALLER performs the return — do not try to bake the return into the helper.

The parallel cycle call site (1993) has redundant logic: it passes the literal "fixer" to review_fix_cycle_limit_reached AND separately scans group.steps for agent=="fixer". When generalizing, fold both into a per-step scan over group.steps so each agent id is checked against the bound table, otherwise grade-retry agents in a parallel group would bypass the bound.

Generalizing changes the event payload `limit` string (from the literal "max_review_fix_cycles" to a per-bound label). Tests/assertions that match on event.payload["limit"] (e.g. the max_agent_steps assertion at src/app/mod.rs:8076) and any review-fix event assertions must be kept aligned.
Limit::Value(0) is rejected at deserialize time (config/mod.rs:131-135) — any new max_grade_retry_cycles default must be a positive Value or Unlimited; 0 is not representable.

review_fix_cycle_count counts reviewer->fixer in ORDER over agent_results, resetting saw_open after each close. A generalized cycle_count must preserve this single-pass reset semantics so interleaved reviewer/grader/fixer sequences are attributed to the correct bound (the open_agent flag is per-bound, so call cycle_count once per bound rather than sharing one flag).

signatures.name: build_clarification_answer — TUI selected-option path that populates selected_option_id from option.id
Complete / Failed arms of handle_orchestrator_decision (templates the accept/abort branches must mirror)
review_fix_cycle_limit_reached / stop_for_review_fix_cycle_limit (the grade-exhaustion site that today stops at LimitReached)
review_fix_cycle_count — the cycle counter retry must reset (derived from run.previous_results)

how_it_works: The clarification transport is a full multi-option picker today, not just free text. The orchestrator emits a WaitingForUser decision carrying clarifying_options: Vec<ClarificationOption> (each {id, label, description}), recommended_option_id, and a multi_select flag (orchestrator/mod.rs:64-83). Validation (orchestrator/mod.rs:448-478) requires 2-4 options with unique non-empty ids and a recommended_option_id that matches one of them — so accept/retry/abort fits the existing contract directly.

On pause (app/mod.rs:1895-1926) the WaitingForUser arm clones the whole RunDriveContext into self.pending_clarification = PendingClarification { run }, mints a fresh question_id via new_id(), copies options/recommended_option_id/multi_select into a PendingClarificationView placed in state.pending_clarification, and records a clarification_requested event. The view is what the TUI renders; the private PendingClarification is what holds the resumable run.

The TUI renders options as a focusable single/multi-select list (tui/mod.rs render_clarification_composer / clarification_key_command). On submit, build_clarification_answer (tui/mod.rs:2096-2176) sets selected_option_id = Some(option.id) and answer = option.label for the focused real option (answer_source "recommended"), or leaves selected_option_id = None with answer_source "custom" for free text. So a user choosing a named option already returns its stable id over the wire.

resolve_pending_clarification (app/mod.rs:1689-1736) is where the answer is consumed. It validates question_id match and non-empty answer, take()s the PendingClarification, records a clarification_answered event (which already logs selected_option_id, but never branches on it), then unconditionally does run.prompt = format!("{}\n\nUser clarification: {}", run.prompt, answer.answer), sets RunState::Planning, and drive_and_replay(run, None). Every answer currently funnels into the same append-and-re-drive path regardless of which option was picked.

Grade/cycle exhaustion today does NOT use this transport. review_fix_cycle_limit_reached (app/mod.rs:3704) checks limits.max_review_fix_cycles against review_fix_cycle_count(run.previous_results) (a reviewer-then-fixer pair counter, app/mod.rs:6019-6033). When hit (call sites app/mod.rs:1977-1980 and 1993-1998), stop_for_review_fix_cycle_limit just sets RunState::LimitReached and records run_limit_reached — a hard stop with no user choice.

The Complete and Failed decision arms (app/mod.rs:1927-1949) are the exact templates for the accept and abort outcomes: Complete sets RunState::Completed + record_workflow_completed(run,false) + run_completed event; Failed sets RunState::Failed + record_workflow_completed + run_failed event.
escalation.design_recommendation:
Reuse the clarification transport end-to-end; do not invent a new pause mechanism. (1) ESCALATE INSTEAD OF STOP: replace the two hard-stop call sites at app/mod.rs:1977-1980 and 1993-1998 (and the body of stop_for_review_fix_cycle_limit at 3704-3724) with a WaitingForUser-style pause. Mirror the WaitingForUser arm (1895-1926): store self.pending_clarification = Some(PendingClarification { run: run.clone() }); build a PendingClarificationView with question_id = new_id(), a question like 'Review/fix cycle limit reached — what should I do?', and three ClarificationOptions with STABLE ids 'accept' / 'retry' / 'abort' (recommended_option_id = 'abort' or 'accept', multi_select = false); record an escalation/clarification_requested event; set RunState::WaitingForUser; return Ok(false). Because the TUI already maps a focused option to selected_option_id = option.id (tui/mod.rs:2152-2161), no TUI change is required — the three ids arrive verbatim. (2) BRANCH IN resolve_pending_clarification BEFORE THE PROMPT-APPEND: insert the tri-state branch between the clarification_answered record_event (ends app/mod.rs:1725) and the unconditional 'let mut run = pending.run; run.prompt = format!(...)' at 1727-1728. Match on answer.selected_option_id.as_deref(): 
- Some("accept") => mirror the Complete arm (1927-1937): self.state.run_state = RunState::Completed; self.record_workflow_completed(&pending.run, false)?; record a run_completed event; clear state.pending_clarification; publish_state(); return Ok(()) WITHOUT re-driving. 
- Some("abort") => mirror the Failed arm (1939-1949): RunState::Failed; record_workflow_completed; run_failed event (reason 'user aborted on cycle exhaustion'); clear pending; publish_state(); return Ok(()) WITHOUT re-driving. 
- Some("retry") => RESET THE CYCLE then drive: take pending.run as mut, trim the review/fix history so review_fix_cycle_count() falls back under max_review_fix_cycles (e.g. retain only non reviewer/fixer agent_results in run.previous_results, or drop the trailing reviewer→fixer pairs) — this is required or the next fixer routing will immediately re-trip review_fix_cycle_limit_reached and re-escalate in a loop; set RunState::Planning; publish_state(); drive_and_replay(run, None). 
- None / any other id / free-text => preserve TODAY'S behavior exactly: fall through to the existing append-and-re-drive (1727-1734), so ordinary clarifications are unaffected. Gate the accept/retry/abort interpretation on the escalation context (e.g. a flag/marker on PendingClarification, or a reserved question namespace) so a normal clarification that happens to use the literal id 'retry' is not hijacked. (3) Keep the trim logic next to review_fix_cycle_count (app/mod.rs:6019) so the reset and the counter stay in sync. This adds the tri-state with zero new transport surface: one new escalation emit site, one new branch before line 1727, and a small previous_results reset helper.
gotchas: There is NO existing accept/retry/abort path — grade exhaustion currently dead-ends at RunState::LimitReached (stop_for_review_fix_cycle_limit, app/mod.rs:3712); the tri-state is net-new behavior layered on the existing pause transport.

selected_option_id is already plumbed through the wire and logged in the clarification_answered event (app/mod.rs:1721) but is never read for control flow — resolve_pending_clarification ignores it and always appends + re-drives. That ignored field is exactly the hook to branch on.

resolve_pending_clarification rejects an empty answer (app/mod.rs:1705-1707). Since build_clarification_answer sets answer = option.label for a chosen option, accept/retry/abort options must have non-empty labels or the answer will be rejected before the branch runs.

The retry branch MUST mutate run.previous_results to drop the cycle count below max_review_fix_cycles. review_fix_cycle_limit_reached re-checks on the very next fixer routing (app/mod.rs:1977, 1993); without a reset, retry re-escalates immediately — an infinite escalation loop.

Reserve/namespace the accept/retry/abort ids so they are only interpreted as control verbs in the escalation context. A normal orchestrator clarification could legitimately use an option labelled/ided 'retry'; without a context gate, branching purely on selected_option_id would mis-route it.

accept/abort branches must NOT call drive_and_replay (the run is terminal) and must clear self.pending_clarification + self.state.pending_clarification and publish_state(), matching how the Complete/Failed arms leave the app idle. Only the retry branch continues the loop.

Both stop_for_review_fix_cycle_limit call sites return Ok(false) inside handle_single_agent_decision / handle_parallel_group_decision; converting them to an escalation must keep returning Ok(false) (pause), not Ok(true) (continue), so drive_and_replay stops the loop and waits for the user.

The orchestrator's waiting_for_user validation enforces 2-4 options and a recommended_option_id that matches an option (orchestrator/mod.rs:448-478). If you synthesize the escalation view directly in the app (bypassing the orchestrator), you can skip that validator, but keep ids unique and recommended_option_id consistent to match the established contract.

signatures.name: apply_diagnostic (what council/grade-as-diagnostic would do WRONG: lifecycle_key=None)

how_it_works: Single chokepoint: every state change is written through App::record_event_with_group (src/app/mod.rs:4215). record_event (4164) is a thin wrapper that passes group_id=None. There is no other path into history or the projection — append_event persists, then self.chat_projection.apply_history_event(&event) updates the in-memory projection, sync_chat_items() copies it into AppState, publish_state() pushes it over the watch channel. So a new feature appears in chat purely by (a) emitting a new event kind here and (b) handling it in apply_history_event.

kind is a free-form &str -> stored as HistoryEvent.kind: String (src/history/mod.rs:22); payload is an arbitrary serde_json::Value (line 23). No enum/registry constrains kinds — you invent a string and add a match arm. run_id/group_id/step_id are the structured correlation fields used to build lifecycle keys.

Dispatch is a single match on event.kind.as_str() (projection.rs:59) ending in a catch-all `_ => {}` (line 110) that SILENTLY DROPS unknown kinds. A new kind shows nothing in chat until an explicit arm is added — this is fail-safe but means forgetting the arm = invisible event.

Collapsing is keyed: upsert (1339) looks up input.lifecycle_key in self.index (a BTreeMap<ChatLifecycleKey, usize>). If the key already exists it overwrites the existing item in place (preserving/merging source.event_ids) instead of pushing a new one. So ALL events that build the same ChatLifecycleKey evolve ONE chat item. Items with lifecycle_key: None always push a fresh item (no collapse).

The clarification pair is the canonical evolving-item model: apply_clarification_requested creates the item keyed by Clarification{run_id,question_id}; apply_clarification_answered (1266) re-derives the SAME key, READS the prior item's body via self.index.get(key) -> self.items.get(index) -> item.body.first() to recover earlier content, rebuilds an accumulated body, and upserts under the same key. That read-prior-then-rebuild pattern is exactly what a multi-round grade loop needs.

Body is capped: bounded_body (1914) truncates every item's body to MAX_BODY_LINES = 12 (projection.rs:19) and each line to MAX_SUMMARY_CHARS. An evolving item that appends one line per round must keep rounds within ~12 lines or older rounds get dropped.

is_terminal_run_conclusion (1425) plus the reorder block in upsert (1369-1377) is the precedent for a placeholder item that starts as Running and, on its terminal update, is moved to the end of the list so it renders chronologically. A grade loop wanting the final PASS/FAIL to sit at the bottom would mirror this.

Anti-pattern (council): council_started / council_synthesized / council_completed are routed (projection.rs:98-100) to apply_diagnostic, which upserts with lifecycle_key: None (line 1107). Result: each council phase becomes a SEPARATE Diagnostic chat item that never collapses — the council review is scattered across multiple lines rather than one evolving review item. A grade loop must NOT copy this; it must use a real lifecycle key + dedicated apply arm.
gotchas: The catch-all `_ => {}` at projection.rs:110 silently drops any kind without an explicit arm — a new grade_round event emits to history but renders nothing until you add a match arm. Easy to miss in testing because record_event still succeeds.

ChatItemKind derives PartialOrd/Ord and is embedded inside ChatLifecycleKey::Step and serialized (snake_case). Adding a variant changes Ord ordering and the serde tag surface; also you MUST add the matching slug() arm (mod.rs:232) or it won't compile.

Adding a ChatLifecycleKey variant forces a new arm in item_id() (mod.rs:206) — non-exhaustive match won't compile, which is good, but the id string format must be unique/stable across rounds (rebuild from history must reproduce identical ids).

MAX_BODY_LINES = 12 hard cap via bounded_body: a grade loop with a high max-rounds (>~10) that writes a line per round will lose the earliest rounds. Prefer a compact rolling body (e.g. a status header line + last N round lines) or summarize.

ChatProjection::rebuild (projection.rs:50) replays the entire event log on session load, so apply_grade_round must be a pure function of the event stream — it cannot depend on App state or in-memory-only counters. The round number / max must live in the event payload, not be inferred from wall-clock arrival.

upsert merges source.event_ids from the existing item (1365-1366) so the evolved item keeps provenance of every round's event — good, but means details/source you set on the new ItemInput are unioned, not replaced; build details to reflect the latest round only if you don't want duplicates.

Severity/status transitions are not enforced anywhere; the apply arm is the sole author of status. A retry loop must explicitly choose Running (working/between rounds), Failed (max exhausted), Completed (PASS) — there is no state machine guarding regressions.
chatProjection.design_recommendation: Model the grade/retry loop on the clarification pair, NOT on council. (1) New event kind(s): emit a single `grade_round` kind through App::record_event(Some(run_id), Some(step_id), \"grade_round\", payload, display) at src/app/mod.rs (the only sanctioned path is record_event/record_event_with_group, mod.rs:4164/4215). Payload should carry the structured fields the projection needs so rebuild stays pure: { \"round\": N, \"max_rounds\": M, \"verdict\": \"working\"|\"fail\"|\"pass\", \"feedback\": \"...\", optional \"target_step_id\" }. One kind covering all three states keeps the dispatch arm and lifecycle simple; alternatively split into grade_started/grade_failed/grade_passed, but a single kind with a verdict field is closer to the run_summary precedent (apply_run_summary, projection.rs:1041, branches on kind/fields to pick title/status/severity). (2) New ChatLifecycleKey variant: add `Grade { run_id: String }` (one grading loop per run) or `Grade { run_id: String, target_step_id: String }` if multiple independent loops can run — to src/app/chat/mod.rs:117 enum, plus a matching arm in item_id() at mod.rs:206 (e.g. format!(\"chat:grade:{run_id}\")). Add a `GradeLoop` variant to ChatItemKind (mod.rs:27) and its slug() arm (mod.rs:232). (3) New apply_grade_round arm: register \"grade_round\" => self.apply_grade_round(event) BEFORE the catch-all in apply_history_event (projection.rs:59-110; do NOT let it fall into the council/apply_diagnostic block at 98-109). Implement apply_grade_round by mirroring apply_clarification_answered (projection.rs:1266): build the Grade key, READ the prior item via self.index.get(&key) -> self.items.get(index) -> item.body to recover earlier round lines, append one compact line for the new round (e.g. ChatLineView::warning(format!(\"Round {round}/{max}: FAIL — {feedback}\")) for a fail, ChatLineView::plain(\"Round {round}/{max}: PASS\") for pass), and upsert under the same Grade key so every round collapses into ONE evolving item. Drive status/severity from verdict: working => (Running, Info/Warning), fail with round<max => (Running, Warning), fail with round==max => (Failed, Error), pass => (Completed, Success). Keep total body within MAX_BODY_LINES=12 (projection.rs:19) — if max_rounds can exceed that, keep a header line plus only the most recent rounds. Optionally add the Grade key to is_terminal_run_conclusion's reorder logic (projection.rs:1425) if you want the concluded PASS/FAIL item to drop to chronological bottom like RunSummary. Anti-pattern to avoid: do not route grade events to apply_diagnostic the way council_started/synthesized/completed are (projection.rs:98-100), because apply_diagnostic upserts with lifecycle_key: None (projection.rs:1107) and therefore produces a separate, non-collapsing item per phase.

signatures.name: test precedent: built-in agent available but disabled by default

how_it_works: Config merge order is built-in defaults -> home -> local -> CLI flags. Each TOML file deserializes into RawConfig (every section/field is Option<...>, every Raw struct has #[serde(default)] #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]), then apply_raw merges only the Some(...) fields onto the already-resolved EffectiveConfig. EffectiveConfig itself is NOT Deserialize (derives only Clone/Debug/PartialEq/Eq) — it is built in code (builtin constructor at src/config/mod.rs:892) and mutated by apply_raw. So a new [grading] section needs THREE touch points exactly like features: a resolved GradingConfig field on EffectiveConfig, a RawGradingConfig field on RawConfig, and an apply_raw merge arm.

The bool opt-in precedent is Features.parallel_step_groups (src/config/mod.rs:196-199): a plain bool defaulting to false via derive(Default). Its raw mirror RawFeatures wraps it in Option<bool> (:447-451), and apply_raw copies it only when present (:938-942). Consumers gate behavior on config.features.parallel_step_groups (e.g. src/orchestrator/mod.rs:507 bails when disabled). A [grading].enabled=false default follows this exact shape.

Built-in agents that ship disabled-by-default (librarian :857-873, designer :874-890) set enabled: false in their BuiltinAgent literal AND the init-config scaffold (starter_config_text raw string, :2314-2331) prints `enabled = false` so users see the knob commented-in. Tests assert they are present-but-disabled (:3307-3324). This is the precedent for shipping the grading feature visible-but-off.

Read-only command auto-approval: classify_command (src/actions/mod.rs:371) returns Allow only when is_default_read_only_command (:443) matches a prefix in the allowlist AND has_shell_control_syntax (:486) is false. The allowlist already auto-approves the canonical verify commands the grader would run agent-discovered (`cargo test`, `cargo check`, `cargo build`, `cargo clippy`, `cargo fmt`). decision_for_command (:356) maps Allow->Allowed, Approve->Allowed under Yolo / RequiresApproval under Normal, Deny->Denied.

has_shell_control_syntax means any verify command containing a pipe, redirect, `;`, `&&`/`||`, backtick, subshell `(...)`/`$(...)`, or a newline is treated as NOT read-only and therefore needs approval (or Yolo). A multi-step verify like `cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy && cargo test` will NOT auto-approve because of the `&&`; each leg auto-approves only when issued as a separate single command. This matters for how an agent-discovered verify command should be shaped/split.

Command timeout for any RunCommand is driven by limits.max_command_minutes (default 10 min, src/config/mod.rs:189), converted via command_timeout(...) at the two execution sites in src/app/mod.rs (:2481, :3992). A long verify build/test inherits this 10-minute cap; there is no grading-specific timeout today.
gotchas: EffectiveConfig is NOT Deserialize (derives only Clone/Debug/PartialEq/Eq at src/config/mod.rs:401). Adding a non-Default field requires updating the builtin constructor at src/config/mod.rs:892 or the struct literal won't compile — there is no serde default to fall back on. Also the PartialEq/Eq derive means GradingConfig must be Eq (fine for bool+u32, but no f32/f64 thresholds).

All Raw structs use #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] (RawConfig at :418, RawFeatures at :448). Forgetting it on RawGradingConfig would silently accept typos; including it means a misspelled key under [grading] becomes a hard load error. Tests load via load_from_temp / load_effective_config and will catch this.

Do NOT add a verify_command field — ADR-002 keeps the verify command agent-discovered in V1. There is currently zero verify_command surface in the codebase; the only 'verify' touchpoints are Capability::Verify and the cargo test/check/build/clippy entries in the read-only allowlist (src/actions/mod.rs:449-453).

The auto-approve allowlist matches by PREFIX on a lowercased command and rejects anything with shell-control syntax. A grader running a combined gate like `cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy && cargo test` will NOT auto-approve (the `&&` trips has_shell_control_syntax at src/actions/mod.rs:514); only single commands auto-approve. Spec the verify contract accordingly.

Versioning: this is config-only and does not change schema_version (apply_raw still bails on anything != 1, src/config/mod.rs:910-914). No Cargo.toml/npm version bump is implied by adding an optional section, but any release-time check:versions rules still apply if a version bump rides along.

If grading should be tunable per-preset/agent later, note that presets only carry agent overrides (RawPreset has only `agents`, src/config/mod.rs:435) — a top-level [grading] section is global, consistent with [features]. Don't try to nest it under presets in the MVP.

max_attempts default (2) intentionally mirrors limits.max_review_fix_cycles (default 2). If the team prefers a single knob, the alternative is to reuse limits.max_review_fix_cycles instead of adding grading.max_attempts — but that couples grading to council review-fix semantics, so a dedicated field is the cleaner recommendation.
